anchors.code: j = parse_listitem(ob, doc, data + end, size - end, flags, attribute);
anchors.note: After the definition-term scan, `parse_definition()` passes only the definition-body line to `parse_listitem()`. Here `end == 59`, so the slice is exactly the trailing 5-byte string `:    ` from the 64-byte footnote buffer.

Because this is a definition-list item, `prefix_dt(":    ", 5)` returns 2 and strips the `: ` marker. `parse_listitem()` therefore calls `is_codefence()` on `data + beg`, which is the last 3 bytes of the footnote buffer: three spaces at offsets 61, 62, and 63 of the 64-byte allocation.

The fence probe receives a 3-byte slice of only spaces. The nested optional-space checks consume every byte, so `i` advances from 0 to 3 and now equals `size` before the function looks for a fence character.

Root cause and sink. With `i == size == 3`, the probe slice already points at `ref->contents->data + 61`, so `c = data[i]` dereferences offset 64 of the 64-byte footnote allocation. The only size guard, `i + 2 >= size`, is evaluated too late because the out-of-bounds byte has already been read. This is the saved `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `is_codefence`.
